breaks: The two halves must land together or the fix regresses the thing it was written for. `text-wrap: pretty` on `.hero-note` WITHOUT the non-breaking date does not fix the first-run note - it relocates the break inside the date, to "Yours arrive on 10" / "August 2026.", which is worse than the widow it replaced. Measured at all four widths. With both halves the note reads "...Yours arrive on" / "10 August 2026." and stays at 3 lines. Re-measure after it lands: (1) line counts, since `pretty` can add a line by rebalancing the tail - it does not here (verified identical across 7 states x 4 widths x 2 grounds), but any later copy change can move it, and `.kpi > .t-small` carries `flex: 1 1 auto` so an added line would grow the KPI row; (2) the 259px `.hero-note` measure, since the date becomes one unbreakable 97px token - safe at 390 today and safe for any longer month, but it is now an overflow surface where it was not before; (3) `.ages .band-head .t-head` is a flex item in a wrapping row, where `balance` can interact with shrink-to-fit sizing - its box measured 308px at 390 and 341px at 1440 both before and after, unchanged. Two cheap costs worth accepting knowingly: copying the date out of the page yields NBSPs rather than spaces, and browser find-in-page for "10 August 2026" is not guaranteed to match. Where `balance`/`pretty` are unsupported the declaration degrades to `wrap`, i.e. exactly today's rendering - no fallback needed. Two slips in the write-up, neither load-bearing: the ghost caption's first line is 44 characters, not 45, and "at 768, 900, 1280 and 1440" mixes a frame height into a list of widths - the declared widths are 390/768/1280/1440 and the caption orphan is present at the upper three and absent at 390.
